head: Kagi Mail: new Gmail alternative with no ads opens public beta
dek: Kagi, the company behind a paid search engine and the Orion browser, opened a public beta of Kagi Mail, an email and calendar service with no ads and no user profiling. It costs 99 dollars a year after a 60-day free trial and comes at no extra cost with Kagi Ultimate.
details: You get 50 GB of storage, a @kagimail.com address, unlimited aliases and your own domains. It blocks or proxies tracking pixels, screens unknown senders and shows verified sender logos. Optional AI features sort mail with plain-language rules, flag what needs a reply and answer questions about your emails; one switch turns them all off. It works with mail apps such as Apple Mail and Thunderbird through IMAP, JMAP and CalDAV; Kagi's own phone apps are planned for the third quarter of 2027.
where: Public beta, web plus standard mail apps; no Kagi phone app yet
means: If you want email without ads or tracking pixels and don't mind paying, you can try Kagi Mail for 60 days, though the trial needs a card and there's no end-to-end encryption.
todo: Start the 60-day trial on Kagi's site if you want to test it, and use Apple Mail, Thunderbird or another mail app on your phone until Kagi's own app arrives.
